sentences.text: Based on comparisons with related dinosaurs, Menefeeceratops is estimated to have been 4 to 4.5 meters long.
Menefeeceratops is potentially the oldest known member of both the ceratopsid family and the centrosaurine subfamily.
It remains the only centrosaurine dinosaur described from New Mexico.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — was discovered by Paul Sealey in 1996, mentioned in 1997, but formally named in 2021 by Dalman, Dodson, and colleagues.
This specimen was collected at locality 3033 in Sandoval County, New Mexico.
The holotype was found in greenish-gray mudstone alongside turtle shell fragments and fossilized wood.

Menefeeceratops lived alongside various dinosaurs including the ankylosaur, nodosaurid Invictarx, hadrosaurids like Ornatops, tyrannosaurids like Dynamoterror, and dromaeosaurids similar to Saurornitholestes.
Menefeeceratops is a genus of ceratopsid dinosaur found in the Menefee Formation of New Mexico, USA, and belongs to the family Ceratopsidae and the subfamily Centrosaurinae.

Menefeeceratops lived during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, between 83.5 and 80 million years ago, in what is now North America, with fossil remains found in the Menefee Formation of New Mexico, USA.
